task: Add explicit, signed platform tenant selection so a platform operator can enter one webshop admin context without storefront login or first-tenant fallback.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This transaction changes canonical tenant resolution for privileged platform actors. The selected tenant must be explicit, actor-bound, signed, server-validated and fail closed without weakening customer/store RBAC or pilot acceptance.

acceptanceCriteria: A platform operator can explicitly select a pilot or active webshop from platform administration and enter /admin in that exact tenant context without storefront/customer login.
The selected context is represented by a short-lived signed HttpOnly cookie whose token is bound to both the authenticated platform actor and the exact instance id.
getCurrentWebshopInstance resolves the signed platform selection only after authenticated actor validation and current platform_operators authority, and queries only the exact selected instance.
A valid explicit selection never falls through to a different tenant if the selected instance becomes unavailable; it fails closed to null.
A different authenticated user cannot inherit another platform actor's selected context.
The platform actor can clear the explicit tenant context and return to the tenant-independent platform control center.
Pilot acceptance, merchant RBAC, customer auth, middleware and parked AAL2 enforcement remain unchanged.
invariants: DOMAIN-TENANCY owns tenant selection; identity only proves actor/platform authority.
No first-tenant, first-membership or ambiguous multi-tenant fallback is introduced.
The platform context token is cryptographically distinct from the storefront pilot acceptance token and is never used as storefront acceptance authority.
Cookie selection cannot itself grant platform authority; current platform_operators state is revalidated on resolution.
Configured tenant deployments remain authoritative before platform context resolution.
Normal merchant resolution through role_bindings remains unchanged when no actor-bound platform context exists.

failureModes: A raw instanceId cookie lets the browser choose tenant truth without server proof.
A signed token that contains only instanceId can leak context across subsequent authenticated users on the same browser.
A stale/invalid selected tenant falls through to another membership and silently changes operating scope.
The new admin context accidentally replaces or broadens Preview pilot storefront acceptance.
edgeCases: Platform actor with zero tenant memberships can select an active webshop because platform authority plus explicit target is sufficient.
Platform actor with multiple tenant bindings resolves only the selected instance.
Expired or tampered token is ignored and existing neutral/membership resolution applies.
Valid actor-bound token for an archived/suspended target resolves null rather than another tenant.
Clearing the context removes only the platform tenant cookie and returns to /admin/platform.

alternatives.summary: Reuse the signed Preview pilot acceptance cookie as the normal platform admin tenant selector.
alternatives.reason: Pilot acceptance owns Preview storefront access semantics and reusing it would collapse storefront acceptance with persistent admin operating context.

alternatives.summary: Persist the currently selected tenant on the platform user profile or another database row and resolve it on every admin request.
alternatives.reason: A mutable account-level pointer would outlive the browser workflow, create cross-device hidden state, and make tenant context less explicit than a bounded signed session selection.

alternatives.summary: Add a short-lived actor-bound signed admin context under the canonical instance authority and validate current platform authority on every resolution.
alternatives.reason: This preserves explicit tenant choice, keeps context browser-session bounded, and composes with current identity authority without introducing first-tenant fallback.

specialistReviews.finding: Tenant selection must remain DOMAIN-TENANCY truth and the admin surfaces may only invoke that authority.
specialistReviews.resolution: The signed token primitive lives under src/lib/instances, while the platform server action only validates the requested target and invokes the tenancy capability.

specialistReviews.finding: A signed tenant id alone is still unsafe across users and cannot substitute for current platform authorization.
specialistReviews.resolution: The token binds actor id, instance id and expiry; canonical resolution additionally revalidates the current platform_operators row before honoring the selected target.

specialistReviews.finding: Platform operators need unambiguous visibility of the current tenant and a deterministic path back to tenant-independent operations.
specialistReviews.resolution: The admin shell displays the active webshop for platform actors and exposes an explicit clear-context action that returns to /admin/platform.

challenge.scenario: Actor A selects tenant X, signs out, and Actor B later authenticates in the same browser.
challenge.finding: An instance-only or unbound cookie could silently leak tenant X into Actor B's privileged session.
challenge.resolution: The signed token includes actorId and the reader returns a tenant only when the token actor matches the current authenticated actor exactly.

challenge.scenario: A valid selected tenant becomes archived, suspended, deleted or otherwise unavailable after the context was minted.
challenge.finding: Falling through to another membership would silently change operating scope and could apply actions to the wrong customer.
challenge.resolution: When a valid explicit platform selection exists, canonical resolution performs one exact eligible-instance lookup and returns null directly if that target is unavailable.

challenge.scenario: A platform actor is demoted or removed from platform_operators while an unexpired context cookie remains.
challenge.finding: The cookie must not preserve cross-tenant privilege after server-side role revocation.
challenge.resolution: getCurrentWebshopInstance revalidates the current platform_operators row before resolving the selected instance and fails closed if authority is absent or unreadable.

challenge.scenario: A client tampers with actor id, instance id, expiry or signature in the tenant-context cookie.
challenge.finding: Browser-controlled mutation must never become tenant truth.
challenge.resolution: The token uses a domain-separated HMAC and timingSafeEqual; malformed, expired or signature-invalid tokens resolve to no explicit platform selection.

challenge.scenario: A deployment already has a configured WEBSHOP_INSTANCE_SLUG and a platform context cookie is also present.
challenge.finding: A cross-tenant cookie must not override deployment-bound tenant authority.
challenge.resolution: Configured tenant resolution remains earlier in getCurrentWebshopInstance than platform context resolution, preserving deployment binding precedence.

challenge.scenario: Preview pilot acceptance and normal platform tenant context coexist in the same browser.
challenge.finding: Reusing or merging their semantics could broaden storefront access or make admin context alter shopper acceptance.
challenge.resolution: The platform context has a separate cookie name, signing domain and /admin path; pilot acceptance remains evaluated independently and earlier where applicable.

proofPlan: Add deterministic source-level regression proof for actor-bound signing, expiry/tamper rejection, exact selected-instance resolution, platform revalidation and no fallback.
Prove both platform control-center and webshop-management surfaces expose explicit selection while the admin shell exposes a clear-context return path.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.
Run Incremental Known Failure Replay and existing Control Plane sync/truth gates.
Require exact-head Completion Truth VERIFIED and lifecycle closure before declaring the block complete.

requirements.requirement: Platform authority can explicitly select and clear an actor-bound signed webshop admin context, and canonical tenant resolution honors only that exact validated target without storefront login or ambiguous fallback.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A selected platform tenant context cannot be reused by a different authenticated actor.
An explicit selected tenant that cannot be resolved must not silently fall through to a different tenant.
Storefront pilot acceptance remains a separate authority and is not repurposed as normal admin tenant selection.

notes: Independent MR1 tenant-selection release unit started from main 4f6a638. PR #858 remains parked and read-only. The task exposed an existing Control Plane coverage gap: canonical src/lib/instances/** tenancy paths were not mapped into release-risk subsystem classification; this branch adds that mapping to the existing auth/access risk subsystem without transferring DOMAIN-TENANCY truth ownership.
